title: How radio waves travel
blurb: Line of sight on VHF and UHF, the ionosphere on HF.

lines.caption: Radio waves leave your antenna and travel in nearly straight lines.
On VHF and UHF, the bands a handheld radio uses, that means line of sight.
The signal reaches about as far as the radio horizon. Past that, it heads out into space.
High above us is a region of the atmosphere called the ionosphere.
The ionosphere can reflect HF radio waves, 3 to 30 MHz, back toward the ground.
They come down far beyond the horizon. Long-distance contacts are far more common on HF.
VHF and UHF signals usually are not sent back by the ionosphere, so they are rarely heard beyond the horizon.
So think of VHF and UHF for local contacts, and HF for long distance.
